NASB.1: Now it came about after these things that Joseph was told, 'Behold, your father is sick.' So he took his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim with him.
NASB.2: When it was told to Jacob, 'Behold, your son Joseph has come to you,' Israel collected his strength and sat up in the bed.
NASB.3: Then Jacob said to Joseph, 'God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
NASB.4: and He said to me, 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and numerous, and I will make you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your descendants after you for an everlasting possession.'
NASB.5: 'Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are.
NASB.6: 'But your offspring that have been born after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the names of their brothers in their inheritance.
NASB.7: 'Now as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died, to my sorrow, in the land of Canaan on the journey, when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).'
NASB.8: When Israel saw Joseph's sons, he said, 'Who are these?'
NASB.9: Joseph said to his father, 'They are my sons, whom God has given me here.' So he said, 'Bring them to me, please, that I may bless them.'
NASB.10: Now the eyes of Israel were [so] dim from age [that] he could not see. Then Joseph brought them close to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
NASB.11: Israel said to Joseph, 'I never expected to see your face, and behold, God has let me see your children as well.'
NASB.12: Then Joseph took them from his knees, and bowed with his face to the ground.
NASB.13: Joseph took them both, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel's right, and brought them close to him.
NASB.14: But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, crossing his hands, although Manasseh was the firstborn.
NASB.15: He blessed Joseph, and said, 'The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, The God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,
NASB.16: The angel who has redeemed me from all evil, Bless the lads; And may my name live on in them, And the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; And may they grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.'
NASB.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, it displeased him; and he grasped his father's hand to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
NASB.18: Joseph said to his father, 'Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn. Place your right hand on his head.'
NASB.19: But his father refused and said, 'I know, my son, I know; he also will become a people and he also will be great. However, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his descendants shall become a multitude of nations.'
NASB.20: He blessed them that day, saying, 'By you Israel will pronounce blessing, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh!'' Thus he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
NASB.21: Then Israel said to Joseph, 'Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you, and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
NASB.22: 'I give you one portion more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and my bow.'

ESV.1: After this, Joseph was told, “Behold, your father is ill.” So he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
ESV.2: And it was told to Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to you.” Then Israel summoned his strength and sat up in bed.
ESV.3: And Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty  appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
ESV.4: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples and will give this land to your offspring after you for an everlasting possession.’
ESV.5: And now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are.
ESV.6: And the children that you fathered after them shall be yours. They shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
ESV.7: As for me, when I came from Paddan, to my sorrow Rachel died in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still some distance  to go to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).”
ESV.8: When Israel saw Joseph's sons, he said, “Who are these?”
ESV.9: Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” And he said, “Bring them to me, please, that I may bless them.”
ESV.10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim with age, so that he could not see. So Joseph brought them near him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
ESV.11: And Israel said to Joseph, “I never expected to see your face; and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
ESV.12: Then Joseph removed them from his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
ESV.13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near him.
ESV.14: And Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands (for Manasseh was the firstborn).
ESV.15: And he blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life long to this day,
ESV.16: the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the boys; and in them let my name be carried on, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude  in the midst of the earth.”
ESV.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him, and he took his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
ESV.18: And Joseph said to his father, “Not this way, my father; since this one is the firstborn, put your right hand on his head.”
ESV.19: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be great. Nevertheless, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude  of nations.”
ESV.20: So he blessed them that day, saying, “By you Israel will pronounce blessings, saying, ‘God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh.’”  Thus he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
ESV.21: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you again to the land of your fathers.
ESV.22: Moreover, I have given to you rather than to your brothers one mountain slope  that I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and with my bow.”

NKJV.1: Now it came to pass after these things that Joseph was told, “Indeed your father is sick”; and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
NKJV.2: And Jacob was told, “Look, your son Joseph is coming to you”; and Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
NKJV.3: Then Jacob said to Joseph: “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
NKJV.4: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a multitude of people, and give this land to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.’
NKJV.5: And now your two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.
NKJV.6: Your offspring whom you beget after them shall be yours; they will be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
NKJV.7: But as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was but a little distance to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).”
NKJV.8: Then Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these?”
NKJV.9: And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place.” And he said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”
NKJV.10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim with age, so that he could not see. Then Joseph brought them near him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
NKJV.11: And Israel said to Joseph, “I had not thought to see your face; but in fact, God has also shown me your offspring!”
NKJV.12: So Joseph brought them from beside his knees, and he bowed down with his face to the earth.
NKJV.13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near him.
NKJV.14: Then Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
NKJV.15: And he blessed Joseph, and said: “God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, The God who has fed me all my life long to this day,
NKJV.16: The Angel who has redeemed me from all evil, Bless the lads; Let my name be named upon them, And the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; And let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.”
NKJV.17: Now when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him; so he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
NKJV.18: And Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”
NKJV.19: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his descendants shall become a multitude of nations.”
NKJV.20: So he blessed them that day, saying, “By you Israel will bless, saying, ‘May God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh!’ ” And thus he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
NKJV.21: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
NKJV.22: Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and my bow.”

CSB17.1: Some time after this, Joseph was told, “Your father is weaker.” So he set out with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
CSB17.2: When Jacob was told, “Your son Joseph has come to you,” Israel summoned his strength and sat up in bed.
CSB17.3: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty <sup>ⓖ</sup> appeared to me at Luz <sup>ⓗ</sup> in the land of Canaan and blessed me.
CSB17.4: He said to me, ‘I will make you fruitful and numerous; I will make many nations come from you, and I will give this land as a permanent possession <sup>ⓘ</sup> to your future descendants.’ <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.5: Your two sons <sup>ⓚ</sup> born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt are now mine. <sup>ⓛ</sup> Ephraim and Manasseh belong to me just as Reuben and Simeon do.
CSB17.6: Children born to you after them will be yours and will be recorded under the names of their brothers with regard to their inheritance.
CSB17.7: When I was returning from Paddan, to my sorrow Rachel died along the way, <sup>ⓜ</sup> some distance from Ephrath in the land of Canaan. I buried her there along the way to Ephrath” (that is, Bethlehem).
CSB17.8: When Israel saw Joseph’s sons, he said, “Who are these?”
CSB17.9: And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons God has given me here.” So Israel said, “Bring them to me and I will bless them.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.10: Now his eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly <sup>[1]</sup> see. <sup>ⓐ</sup> Joseph brought them to him, and he kissed and embraced them. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.11: Israel said to Joseph, “I never expected to see your face again, but now God has even let me see your offspring.”
CSB17.12: Then Joseph took them from his father’s knees and bowed with his face to the ground. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.13: Then Joseph took them both — with his right hand Ephraim toward Israel’s left, and with his left hand Manasseh toward Israel’s right — and brought them to Israel.
CSB17.14: But Israel stretched out his right hand and put it on the head of Ephraim, the younger, and crossing his hands, put his left on Manasseh’s head, although Manasseh was the firstborn. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.15:
Then he blessed Joseph and said: The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, ⓔ
the God who has been my shepherd ⓕ all my life to this day,
CSB17.16:
the angel who has redeemed me from all harm ⓖ  —
may he bless these boys.
And may they be called by my name
and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, ⓗ
and may they grow to be numerous within the land.
CSB17.17: When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, he thought it was a mistake <sup>[2]</sup> and took his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s.
CSB17.18: Joseph said to his father, “Not that way, my father! This one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.”
CSB17.19: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know! He too will become a tribe, <sup>[3]</sup> and he too will be great; nevertheless, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a populous nation.” <sup>[4]</sup>
CSB17.20: So he blessed them that day, putting Ephraim before Manasseh when he said, “The nation Israel will invoke blessings by you, saying, ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’”
CSB17.21: Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.22: Over and above what I am giving your brothers, I am giving you the one mountain slope <sup>[5]</sup> that I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow.” <sup>ⓙ</sup>

NLT.1: One day not long after this, word came to Joseph, “Your father is failing rapidly.” So Joseph went to visit his father, and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
NLT.2: When Joseph arrived, Jacob was told, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” So Jacob gathered his strength and sat up in his bed.
NLT.3: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me.
NLT.4: He said to me, ‘I will make you fruitful, and I will multiply your descendants. I will make you a multitude of nations. And I will give this land of Canaan to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.’
NLT.5: “Now I am claiming as my own sons these two boys of yours, Ephraim and Manasseh, who were born here in the land of Egypt before I arrived. They will be my sons, just as Reuben and Simeon are.
NLT.6: But any children born to you in the future will be your own, and they will inherit land within the territories of their brothers Ephraim and Manasseh.
NLT.7: “Long ago, as I was returning from Paddan-aram, Rachel died in the land of Canaan. We were still on the way, some distance from Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem). So with great sorrow I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath.”
NLT.8: Then Jacob looked over at the two boys. “Are these your sons?” he asked.
NLT.9: “Yes,” Joseph told him, “these are the sons God has given me here in Egypt.” And Jacob said, “Bring them closer to me, so I can bless them.”
NLT.10: Jacob was half blind because of his age and could hardly see. So Joseph brought the boys close to him, and Jacob kissed and embraced them.
NLT.11: Then Jacob said to Joseph, “I never thought I would see your face again, but now God has let me see your children, too!”
NLT.12: Joseph moved the boys, who were at their grandfather’s knees, and he bowed with his face to the ground.
NLT.13: Then he positioned the boys in front of Jacob. With his right hand he directed Ephraim toward Jacob’s left hand, and with his left hand he put Manasseh at Jacob’s right hand.
NLT.14: But Jacob crossed his arms as he reached out to lay his hands on the boys’ heads. He put his right hand on the head of Ephraim, though he was the younger boy, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, though he was the firstborn.
NLT.15:
Then he blessed Joseph and said, “May the God before whom my grandfather Abraham
and my father, Isaac, walked —
the God who has been my shepherd
all my life, to this very day,
NLT.16:
the Angel who has redeemed me from all harm —
may he bless these boys.
May they preserve my name
and the names of Abraham and Isaac.
And may their descendants multiply greatly
throughout the earth.”
NLT.17: But Joseph was upset when he saw that his father placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head. So Joseph lifted it to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
NLT.18: “No, my father,” he said. “This one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.”
NLT.19: But his father refused. “I know, my son; I know,” he replied. “Manasseh will also become a great people, but his younger brother will become even greater. And his descendants will become a multitude of nations.”
NLT.20: So Jacob blessed the boys that day with this blessing: “The people of Israel will use your names when they give a blessing. They will say, ‘May God make you as prosperous as Ephraim and Manasseh.’” In this way, Jacob put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
NLT.21: Then Jacob said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will take you back to Canaan, the land of your ancestors.
NLT.22: And beyond what I have given your brothers, I am giving you an extra portion of the land that I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow.”

WEB.3: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
WEB.4: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your offspring  after you for an everlasting possession.’
WEB.5: Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, will be mine.
WEB.6: Your issue, whom you become the father of after them, will be yours. They will be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
WEB.7: As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).”
WEB.8: Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these?”
WEB.9: Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” He said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”
WEB.10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he couldn’t see. He brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
WEB.11: Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring  also.”
WEB.12: Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
WEB.13: Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near to him.
WEB.14: Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
WEB.15: He blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day,
WEB.16: the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Let them grow into a multitude upon the earth.”
WEB.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
WEB.18: Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”
WEB.19: His father refused, and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also will be great. However, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring  will become a multitude of nations.”
WEB.20: He blessed them that day, saying, “In you will Israel bless, saying, ‘God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh’” He set Ephraim before Manasseh.
WEB.21: Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
WEB.22: Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”

AMP.1: Now some time after these things happened, Joseph was told, "Your father is sick." So he took his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim with him [to go to Goshen].
AMP.2: And when Jacob (Israel) was told, "Look now, your son Joseph has come to you," Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
AMP.3: Then Jacob said to Joseph, " God Almighty appeared to me at Luz (Bethel) in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
AMP.4: and said to me, 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and numerous, and I will make you a great company of people, and will give this land to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.'
AMP.5: Now your two sons [Ephraim and Manasseh], who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine [that is, adopted as my heirs and sons as surely], as Reuben and Simeon are my sons.
AMP.6: But other sons who were born to you after them shall be your own; they shall be called by the names of their [two] brothers in their inheritance.
AMP.7: Now as for me, when I came from Paddan [in Mesopotamia], Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan on the journey, when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)."
AMP.8: When Israel [who was almost blind] saw Joseph's sons, he said, "Who are these?"
AMP.9: Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here [in Egypt]." So he said, "Please bring them to me, so that I may bless them."
AMP.10: Now Israel's eyes were so dim from age that he could not see [clearly]. Then Joseph brought them close to him, and he kissed and embraced them.
AMP.11: Israel said to Joseph, "I never expected to see your face, but see, God has shown me your children as well."
AMP.12: Then Joseph took the boys [from his father's embrace], and he bowed [before him] with his face to the ground.
AMP.13: Then Joseph took them both, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel's right, and brought them close to him.
AMP.14: But Israel reached out his right hand and laid it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, crossing his hands [intentionally], even though Manasseh was the firstborn.
AMP.15:
Then Jacob (Israel) blessed Joseph, and said,
"The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked [in faithful obedience],
The God who has been my Shepherd [leading and caring for me] all my life to this day,
AMP.16:
The Angel [that is, the LORD Himself] who has redeemed me [continually] from all evil,
Bless the boys;
And may my name live on in them [may they be worthy of having their names linked with mine],
And the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac;
And may they grow into a [great] multitude in the midst of the earth."
AMP.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, it displeased him [because he was not the firstborn]; and he grasped his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
AMP.18: Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father, for this is the firstborn; place your right hand on Manasseh's head."
AMP.19: But his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know; Manasseh also will become a people and he will be great; but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his descendants shall become a multitude of nations."
AMP.20:
Then Jacob blessed them that day, saying,
"By you Israel will pronounce a blessing, saying,
'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'"
And he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
AMP.21: Then Israel said to Joseph, "Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you, and bring you back to [Canaan] the land of your fathers.
AMP.22: Moreover, I have given you [the birthright,] one portion [Shechem, one mountain ridge] more than any of your brothers, which I took [reclaiming it] from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and with my bow."
